messages:
olga: Heads up — after yesterday's continuous-batcher tweak we saw a p95 jump on small requests around 07:14 UTC. Looks like a microburst -> kernel cascade plus KV prefill thrash. p95 small-token went ~45ms -> ~220ms.

sam: Which hosts / model? can you paste the quick stats?

olga: model: redwood-open-3b, region: us-west-2, hosts: dedicated-pool-3. Quick snapshot from the dashboards: 
```
batch_size_histogram = {1: 72%, 2: 15%, 4+: 13%}
kernel_fallback_count = +300/min (post-tweak)
kv_prefill_ops = +4.5x
kv_lock_wait_p95 = 120ms (was 8ms)
cpu% agent = steady
gpu_util = slightly down
```

priya: That kv_lock_wait p95 is the smoking gun. If prefill rate jumps it can thrash the prefix/KV priming and hold locks which stalls the fast-path kernel. Did the heuristic change lower the token-budget floor?

olga: Yes — config delta: `continuous_batcher.token_budget_target` went 32 -> 20 for the small-batch optimization, plus we relaxed `packlet_merge_threshold` so small microbatches merge less aggressively.

kai: I ran a short perf trace on a repro host. TL;DR: lots of tiny batches hit the slow kernel selection path which then schedules a prefill for each microbatch. Prefill + lock contention = cascade. Snip from trace (condensed):
```
[07:14:03] recv small req (tokens=6)
[07:14:03.002] batcher: form batch size=1 -> select kernel slow_path_v2
[07:14:03.004] kv: need_prefill -> start prefill shard A
[07:14:03.020] kernel exec delayed waiting on kv_lock (wait=18ms)
[07:14:03.040] other tiny req arrives -> triggers another prefill -> kv_lock queue grows
```

jen: Sounds convincing. Canary rollback to previous token_budget_target = 32? We should confirm perf recovers before more wide rollout.

ci-bot: @jen initiated rollback: deploy continuous-batcher-config -> v1.18.3 (rollback) to pool dedicated-pool-3. Status: rolling. :gear:

len: Quick thought — two mitigations that are low-risk:
- Raise a `min_batch_tokens` floor so we avoid too many single-token batches (e.g., min_batch_tokens=16).
- Add a lightweight prefill debounce: if a prefill for a cache shard started in the last X ms, join it instead of starting another.

sam: I can run an A/B canary: pool A = rollback (token_budget_target=32), pool B = keep tweak + min_batch_tokens=16 + prefill-debounce=50ms. We'll collect p50/p95 and kv_lock_wait.

priya: Also check kernel selection metrics: we need to compare fraction of requests hitting `fast_path_v1` vs `slow_path_v2`. If small-batch heuristic shifts >60% to slow_path that's bad.

olga: For triage notes:
- Probable cause: token_budget_target reduction -> more single/micro batches -> kernel choose slower path optimized for different shape -> each triggers KV prefill -> KV lock contention -> overall latency cascade.
- Immediate mitigation: rollback config + apply min_batch_tokens on experiments.
- Longer term: make kernel selection prefer fast path if request size < X and prefer shared prefill.

jen: +1 on rollover. Assigning owners: rollback/monitor = @ci-bot/@jen, canary experiment = @sam, KV prefill/debounce design = @priya, kernel-selection followup = @kai, postmortem if confirmed = @olga.

olga: Thanks — I'll collect traces and p95 graphs after rollback completes and post summary. If rollback doesn't fully recover we'll flip the canary to the min_batch_tokens variant.

ci-bot: Rollback complete on dedicated-pool-3. Post-rollback quick check: p95 small-token -> 48ms, kv_lock_wait_p95 -> 9ms. Rolling up full metrics to #eng-runtime-daily.

sam: Nice. I'll start the canary A/B tomorrow for 3 hours and report back with perf + allocation delta.

olga: Closing loop later today — thanks everyone. :seedling:
